::: {#exm-racket-traversals}
#### The three traversals in Racket

These functions follow the definitions of preorder (@def-preorder), inorder (@def-inorder) and postorder (@def-postorder),
with `B` as in @exr-racket-tree:

```{racket}
#| code-fold: false
(define (preorder T)
  (if (empty? T)
      empty
      (cons (first T)
            (append (preorder (second T)) (preorder (third T))))))

(define (inorder T)
  (if (empty? T)
      empty
      (append (inorder (second T))
              (cons (first T) (inorder (third T))))))

(define (postorder T)
  (if (empty? T)
      empty
      (append (postorder (second T))
              (postorder (third T))
              (list (first T)))))
```

`(append L M N)` is the list of the elements of `L`, then `M`, then `N`.
The three traversals of `B` are:

```{racket}
#| code-fold: false
(preorder B)
(inorder B)
(postorder B)
```

:::
